caveats: This is the untrained model's result first. Whether the Tinker-trained proposers beat random edits across layers is not settled: 74 of 222 proposed edits have been scored so far, and in layer 23 a random row swap also works.
The edit removes one habit; it does not add math ability. Banning the "Wait" token, with no weight change, scores the same (Beaker's finding).

We chose what the proposer sees: the six tokens of the table include the two "Wait" tokens, and the prompt names the failure. The proposer chose the layer rows, the direction and the size of the change.
One model, one failure mode, one sampled answer per problem (the published protocol averages four). The published edit and the token ban were run on 250 of the 500 problems here.
The two edits given the full MATH-500 run were picked by their score on 256 held-out practice problems before layers 16-21 had been screened.
For reference, not re-run here: Takehi et al. report 48.1% for GPT-6 Astra's edit with 50 forward passes (51.1% in Beaker's re-run); Beaker's best runs reach 37.4-39.5%.
summary: Qwen3.5-0.8B loops on lines that start with "Wait" and runs out of tokens: unedited it solves 8.2% of MATH-500. We showed Inkling 2 Small one MLP layer of Qwen as a small table read from the weights (six tokens by 64 neurons) and wrote its answer into the real model. The best edit so far, proposed by the untrained model with reasoning, scales down layer 23's push on the two "Wait" tokens and reaches 38.2% [34.0, 42.4] (+30.0 points [+25.8, +34.2] paired against unedited). On the 250 problems where both were run it is level with the published one-neuron edit (+2.4 points [-3.6, +8.4]), and banning the "Wait" token without touching any weight does as well. In layer 23, 15 of 16 single answers from our two RL-trained proposers helped on practice problems (no reasoning, about 137 output tokens each; one of their edits is in the table), against 7 of 8 from the untrained model with reasoning (about 1,685 tokens each), 2 of 8 random edits, and none from the untrained model without reasoning, which never produced a valid answer. That is one layer; the other layers are still being scored.
